correctness.rationale: All edges of both cubic families have four distinct adjacent edges. Two named colours therefore force the exact 2-of-4 linear equations for a_i,b_i,c_i. Subtraction gives d_{i+2}=-d_i and s_{i-1}+s_i=2; the identically-equal rim case contradicts the rung equations, so b_i=1-a_i, a_{i+2}=1-a_i, c_{i+1}=1-c_i. The rim's least period is four. An ordinary seam requires 4|n, a twisted seam n=2 mod 4; three independent initial bits give exactly eight label-sensitive indexed assignments. Proper 3-edge-colourings of both cubic families yield strong-majority 3-colour upper bounds even where 2 impossible; one colour is impossible with nonzero adjacency. Direct unrelated enumeration used actual edge-neighbour sets of constructed indexed graphs and found P3=0,P4=8,P5=0,P6=0,P8=8 and M4=8,M6=0,M8=0,M10=0,M12=8. Bounds n=3 and n=2, K4 case, seams and colour-name convention checked. Infinite conclusion is from recurrence, not finite counts.

final_claim: For P_n=C_n square K_2 (n>=3), Maj' is 2 iff n=0 mod 4 and otherwise 3; for M_{2n} (n>=2), Maj' is 2 iff n=2 mod 4 and otherwise 3. Each two-colourable indexed graph has exactly eight assignments with two named colours.
